subject: Request: Traffic rescue safety authorization for FastFin pilot
messages:
From: Elaine Morris <elaine@fastfin.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Traffic rescue safety authorization for FastFin pilot

Hi Tessa,

Quick note from our side — we’re ready to flip on a controlled canary for the FastFin Payments pilot starting tomorrow (Wed 6/16). Because this model change touches payment-fraud routing, our legal and ops teams want an explicit safety plan from Redwood that includes: an automatic rollback trigger if latency or error metrics degrade beyond agreed thresholds, and a short-duration sticky-version (pin) to prevent flapping during immediate post-failure triage.

We understand this may require a temporary SLO carveout or exception. Attached is our latest Mutual Action Plan (FastFin_MAP_v2.pdf). Can Redwood approve a contingency flow and sign-off on the conditions below by EOD today? We need to confirm to our CISO.

Requested (high level):
- Canary width: ~3% of production traffic for 6 hours
- Auto-fallback when p95 latency > 450ms OR error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes
- If fallback occurs, allow a sticky version (pin) for up to 48 hours while we triage together

Please let me know what you need from us; happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Elaine Morris
Director, Platform Reliability
FastFin Payments

Attachments: FastFin_MAP_v2.pdf
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Traffic rescue safety authorization for FastFin pilot

Looping you both in — Elaine sent the MAP and wants a formal failover+pin flow for the pilot. Quick draft of what I think we can offer:

Proposal (draft):
- Canary width: 3% traffic, 6-hour window (as requested)
- Telemetry: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5m error rate, throughput — ship dashboard (see attached slo_dashboard_q2.png)
- Auto-fallback rule: trigger when p95 > 450ms OR error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 consecutive minutes
- Post-fallback sticky-version (pin): allow up to 24 hours by default; manual extension possible with SRE+Eng approval to reach 48h max
- Guardrails: canary limited to non-peak hours for first 24h, SRE on-call monitoring required; limit concurrent canaries to 1 in region

Questions for you:
1) Is 24h pin + manual extension acceptable from an engineering risk perspective (vs their 48h ask)?
2) Can we commit to an immediate auto-unpin when metrics return stable for two consecutive 1-hour windows?
3) Any legal/contracting flags we should surface before we tell FastFin yes?

If you’re good with this, I’ll send Elaine a concise confirmation and request their CISO to acknowledge.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Lead (Payments)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: slo_dashboard_q2.png
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Traffic rescue safety authorization for FastFin pilot

Thanks for the summary, Tessa — technical + ops perspective below. TL;DR: we can support their flow with a few constraints and automated safety mechanisms.

Recommended concrete rules:
- Canary: 3% traffic, 6 hours (same)
- Metric windows: evaluate p95 over 1m rolling, require threshold breach for 5 consecutive 1m windows to reduce noisy flips
- Trigger thresholds: p95 >= 450ms OR error rate >= 0.5% (matches ask)
- Automatic action: immediate traffic shift back to pinned stable variant (0% traffic to canary) plus alert to SRE; preserve KV caches for 2 hours to speed repro vs full cold start
- Pin behavior: allow a system-enforced sticky-version where the canary model remains pinned for up to 48 hours by default, but auto-unpin if both p95 and error rate normalize for 2 consecutive 1-hour aggregates
- Safety caps: pin extensions beyond 48h require explicit approval from Redwood Eng leadership + CS manager

Operational notes:
- We’ll expose a read-only dashboard link to FastFin for the canary window (no access to logs).
- Need procurement/legal to sign a one-off SLA carveout document specifying the temporary mitigation and responsibilities.

If Laura agrees on the 48h pin + auto-unpin behavior, I’ll prepare the operation playbook snippets and the rollback automation patch for deployment tonight.

—Aditya
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Traffic rescue safety authorization for FastFin pilot

Appreciate the quick responses. Engineering stance below — we can greenlight with the following changes to reduce blast radius:

1) Pin window: set default sticky-version limit to 36 hours (compromise between their 48h ask and our ops risk). Any extension beyond 36h requires sign-off from Eng Director + CS lead.
2) Canary timing: prefer non-peak window for the first 6hr run; if they insist on business-hours canary, require SRE presence and a rollback dial available to FastFin immediate-contact.
3) Auto-unpin: require 2 consecutive 30-minute aggregates of stable metrics to unpin automatically (faster recovery than hourly but still conservative).
4) Telemetry hooks: we must get their CISO to sign the minimal telemetry-sharing appendix. No log access, but aggregated metrics as Aditya described.

I’ll approve the plan as long as Aditya pushes the rollback automation tonight and Legal prepares the carveout language. Tessa — please include these conditions in your confirmation and ask for CISO acknowledgment.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Elaine — thanks for the note and the MAP. Quoting your ask below for clarity: 

On Tue, Jun 15, 2026 at 9:07 AM Elaine Morris <elaine@fastfin.com> wrote:
> Quick note from our side — we’re ready to flip on a controlled canary for the FastFin Payments pilot starting tomorrow (Wed 6/16). Because this model change touches payment-fraud routing, our legal and ops teams want an explicit safety plan from Redwood that includes: an automatic rollback trigger if latency or error metrics degrade beyond agreed thresholds, and a short-duration sticky-version (pin) to prevent flapping during immediate post-failure triage.

We can confirm Redwood will support the pilot with the following finalized conditions: 
- Canary width: 3% of production traffic, 6-hour window (first run scheduled for 2026-06-16 non-peak)
- Auto-fallback: immediate rollback to stable variant when p95 >= 450ms OR error rate >= 0.5% sustained for 5 consecutive 1-minute windows (system-enforced)
- Sticky-version (pin): allowed up to 36 hours by default; auto-unpin will occur after 2 consecutive 30-minute aggregates of stable metrics. Extensions beyond 36 hours require explicit sign-off by Redwood Eng Director + CS lead
- Telemetry: aggregated p50/p95/p99 and error-rate dashboards shared read-only with FastFin; no access to raw logs
- Operational guardrails: SRE on-call during the first run; rollback automation will be applied prior to canary start

Next steps for FastFin: please reply with CISO acknowledgment and sign the attached Mutual Action Plan (FastFin_MAP_v2.pdf). Once we receive that, Aditya will deploy the rollback automation and Legal/Procurement will prepare the temporary SLA carveout.

If that matches your expectations, please confirm and we’ll finalize scheduling.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Lead (Payments)
Redwood Inference
